question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2023 Q3c — Latent Heat of Fusion of Ice
question.text:
A thermometer is placed in a plastic cup containing 200 g of water at 22°C. Small pieces of ice at 0°C are added one by one, stirring after each addition, until the thermometer reads 0°C. The total mass of ice added was 60 g.

Specific heat capacity of water: c = 4.2 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹
question.general_feedback:
Model solution:
Step 1 — Thermal energy lost by water:
Q = mcΔT = 200 × 4.2 × (22 − 0) = 200 × 4.2 × 22 = 18 480 J

Step 2 — Specific latent heat of fusion:
L = Q ÷ mice = 18 480 ÷ 60 = 308 J g⁻¹ (= 308 000 J kg⁻¹)

Common errors: using mass of water instead of mass of ice in Step 2; forgetting ΔT = 22°C (not 0°C).

steps.label:
Given: mwater = 200 g  |  Tinitial = 22°C  |  Tfinal = 0°C  |  mice = 60 g
cwater = 4.2 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹  |  Formula: Q = mcΔT    L = Q ÷ mice
Calculate the thermal energy lost by the original volume of water. (3 marks)
Calculate the specific latent heat of fusion of ice. Assume all thermal energy lost by the water was transferred to the ice. (3 marks)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Check: Q = m × c × ΔT. Use m = 200 g (not 60 g), c = 4.2, ΔT = 22.

fields.label: Specific latent heat of fusion L = _____ J g⁻¹
fields.alt_unit_note: Accept 308 000 J/kg if student states kg unit

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Divide the heat lost (Q) by the mass of ice (60 g), not the mass of water.
error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: L = Q ÷ m_ice. The denominator is the mass of ice that melted.
